title: Policy 2021-02 definition and general requirements for every shared pharmacy service model
subtopic: General requirements for shared pharmacy service models
rule_summary: Board Policy 2021-02 (adopted 2/19/21; revised 4/7/22 and 2/6/25) provides minimum standards for Shared Pharmacy Service models involving Massachusetts licensees, and states that, unless otherwise noted, shared service models not addressed in the policy require a petition to the Board for approval. It adopts the NABP definition of Shared Pharmacy Services: a system that allows a participating pharmacist or pharmacy, pursuant to a request from another participating pharmacist or pharmacy, to process or fill a prescription drug order, which may include preparing, packaging, labeling, compounding for specific patients, dispensing, performing drug utilization reviews, conducting claims adjudication, obtaining refill authorizations, reviewing therapeutic interventions, and/or reviewing institutional facility orders. Its general requirements for all models are that: all participants maintain full compliance with federal and state law, including pharmacy licensure and technician supervision requirements (or the state equivalent); shared services occur within the United States; participants have the same owner or a written contract or agreement outlining the services provided and the shared responsibilities of each party; participants share a common electronic file or technology allowing secure access to required information; participants assure data security and protect the confidentiality and integrity of protected health information; no part of the database is duplicated, downloaded, or removed from the pharmacy's electronic database; dispensed medications are pursuant to valid, patient-specific prescriptions or standing orders; pharmacy systems can track and produce an audit trail of the prescription through each step, including at a minimum date/time and individuals involved; each participant is jointly responsible for properly processed and filled prescriptions; initiation or continuation of therapy, quality, or safety is not compromised; retail pharmacies notify patients that their prescriptions may be processed or filled by another pharmacy and provide a mechanism for patients to opt out; all participants have documented training; participants jointly develop, implement, review, revise and comply with joint policies and procedures, each maintaining the portion relating to its operations and including at a minimum those in the Shared Pharmacy Services section of the most recent NABP Model Act; participants review the written policies and procedures at least annually and document the review; pharmacies establish and maintain a continuity of care plan for when any participant cannot process or fill prescriptions; and participants comply with any other requirements the Board deems necessary to protect public health and safety.
exam_relevance: Tests the common safeguards that apply to central fill, remote processing and telepharmacy alike, including patient notice and opt-out, joint responsibility and the annual policy review.

common_confusions: Common ownership and a written agreement are alternatives; separately owned participants need the written contract or agreement.
Joint responsibility means each participant is responsible for properly processed and filled prescriptions; the arrangement does not move all responsibility to one party.
The patient notice and opt-out mechanism are duties of retail pharmacies in the arrangement.
